claim.why_it_matters: ADD GR 1 (standard arithmetic): the subscripts 1, 2 and n on operand-1 are flattened into the name, so the expression reads as operands named operand-11, operand-12 and operand-1n instead of the 1st, 2nd and nth instances of operand-1.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 416 (PDF p438), 14.8.2.3 GR1, shows '(operand-1' followed by lowered subscript glyphs 1, 2 and n: '(operand-1_1 + operand-1_2 + ... + operand-1_n)'. Line 15 of page-438.md reads '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n)'. The subscripts are flattened into the name, so the transcription names different operands (operand-11, operand-12) rather than the 1st, 2nd and nth instances of operand-1. Both sources are quoted correctly. This is a content change, not formatting. The same defect also appears in GR2 (markdown line 27: '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)', printed with subscripts), which the claim does not mention.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate for GR1. The same subscript flattening also occurs in GR2 on this page: the PDF prints '(operand-1_1 + operand-1_2 + ... + operand-1_n + operand-2)' and the markdown has '(operand-11 + operand-12 + ... + operand-1n + operand-2)'.
